items.title: Affinity is coming to Linux (but there’s no ETA yet)
items.content:
It’s official: Affinity , the free design app made by Canva, is coming to Linux.

Replying to users on X asking about possible Linux support, the official account said a version is ‘in active development’, though it doesn’t say when a release might land, or what tooling approach the Linux build will use.

Affinity is owned by Canva, who bought its British developer , Serif, in 2024. They went on to released a revamped v3 of the suite in October 2025, merging three paid apps into a single free app with a unified UI.

Presently, Affinity is available on Windows, macOS and (as of November 3) iPadOS. But while there is no official Linux version right now, today’s news means it’s now a question of when and not want:

Affinity’s reply on X – no walking it back now

You can already run Affinity on Linux via WINE thanks to an unofficial wrapper project. I found that effort impressive, albeit not flawless. There are quirks with signing in to Canva, using hardware acceleration, UI scaling and updates to newer builds.

An official Linux build supported by Canva should mean there are resources to resolve those niggles. And if not? Well, it’s easy to complain at a company with resources, than it is a volunteer working in their free time.

While the announcement of Affinity for Linux is sure to create waves with creatives (many keen to switch from Windows), open-source alternatives to big-tech software don’t vanish once Affinity arrives on Linux.

Having Affinity available won’t mean people stop using Krita or The GIMP or Inkscape or anything else – nor should they. Tools are tools; having the choice to use something is, as I like to say, better than no choice to use it.

Many may prefer to hold out hope that the ArtCraft suite of Adobe software clones, which are being built using LLMs, reach the lofty aims their software factory owner has.

Canva’s Affinity is already real, working software, kitted out with a full toolset people use day-to-day and backed by a company. Established software that runs on Linux makes it easier for people to switch to Linux – and stick with it long term.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임받을 이용자가 [매니저 위임 신청] 버튼으로 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 활동 중인 부매니저가 있으면 부매니저만, 부매니저가 없거나 모두 부재중이면 회원이 신청할 수 있습니다.

신청하면 갤러리 공지로 신청 글이 등록되고, 신청일로부터 7일간 찬성 댓글을 받은 뒤 운영자가 검토해 위임합니다. 첫 번째 위임 신청자가 신청한 날로부터 7일간 3명까지 동시 신청이 가능합니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

items.title: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
items.content:
On affected OpenJDK builds, malformed Base64 data can cause a constant-value overwrite of allocated heap memory. Through remote Heap Feng Shui, we turn that overwrite into a heap leak and remote code execution.

A few months back, I was developing a 0-click exploit on a certain phone vendor. The bug was constrained: it is a linear out-of-bounds write and we have no way to bypass ASLR. I almost considered it unexploitable until I audited the Android Runtime. Turns out, it has some predictable memory allocation pattern and if you align the registers from the starting memory corruption just right you can make the runtime interpret attacker's bytecode.

After completing that exploit chain, inspired (and bored), I decided to look into some thing completely different. So I pulled the official JVM implementation (OpenJDK HotSpot) and started auditing. Java is a mature platform, so I was aware that having a "good" bug here would be hard, but I wanted to give it my best attempt anyway.

Recalling my earlier lesson that complex systems and code crossing multiple boundaries are difficult to get right, I focused the audit on the JIT compiler, intrinsics, widely accessible APIs, and cryptography. Well, more precisely, I told Codex to look at those areas like any serious security researcher in 2026. To be honest, I didn't expect to find anything trivially exploitable, perhaps only some logic flaws or side-channel issues.

Most early results Codex brought me were slops, either unreachable or the requirement of exploitation is not realistic at all. This looks like a gamble I am going to lose. But you know what, fortune favors the bold. So I just prompted harder...

Eventually, Codex brought me a finding for a memory corruption in the Base64 decoder itself. I came looking for copper and found gold, through sheer persistence. But wait, is it really gold, or just fool's gold?

The issue lies in OpenJDK HotSpot's x86-64 Base64 intrinsic. C2 is the most aggressive JIT compiler in the Java Virtual Machine. Specifically, if you trigger a function repeatedly, then it will compile that function into native code. Even then, ordinary native code itself is not fast enough. Modern CPUs have specialized instructions that allow processing data even faster. HotSpot uses them in optimized routines called intrinsics. The x86-64 Base64 intrinsic miscalculated the padded tail's store mask, causing an out-of-bounds write.

The x86-64 Base64 intrinsic iterates through the input in 256-byte blocks; if it is less than 256, then it will do so in 64-byte blocks. When the input is less than 64 bytes, it uses evmovdqub , the intrinsic for the VMOVDQU8 instruction. This instruction takes a 64-bit mask that decides which bytes are read from or written to memory. The mask is first calculated from the input and output length, then updated to reflect the number of padding bytes ( '=' ) in the Base64-encoded string. This is shown in the following (pseudocode):

Copy // Zero High Bits Starting with Specified Bit Position

In the above code, if the remaining input is of the form =, ==, X=, X==, XY= , or === , then output_len will be computed as zero. However, since there is padding, output_len is decremented, resulting in an underflowed value of -1 or -2 . Since bzhiq(-1, output_len) doesn’t change any bits if output_len >= 64 , this results in output_mask == -1u64 .

Later the code uses evmovdqub to read and write multiple bytes at a time. For a write, if the mask bit is 1 , the byte at that index in the vector register is written to memory. So when output_mask == -1u64 , all 64 bytes are written during the following operation:

items.title: Actual curl rewrites in rust
items.content:
For a long time we have received repeated requests for, or questions about, a curl rewrite in rust. Often as a joke, but also seriously.

In this modern world of AIs, we have only been waiting for someone to prove it possible and now it seems we don’t have to wait anymore.

This fall seems to be the time of the curl-in-rust takes as we first saw urlx appear a few months ago, claimed to be a memory-safe, from-scratch reimplementation of curl and libcurl and now in November curl, rewritten in Rust – a rewrite of curl and libcurl in Rust . This second one confusingly enough not even using a different name.

This latter one claims to have spent 8,600 USD to make it happen.

Writing code once was never the big deal with software and it still isn’t. Sure, it’s fascinating that you can make a set of agents accomplish this in only a few weeks but let’s face it: it could do this because all the AIs of the world have trained on curl code for years. curl is extremely well documented, there are hundreds of existing open source application using its API and there are thousands of test cases to verify the implementation.

The C code sits there and all the AI needs to do is convert it to rust, then polish until the tests work.

A know-it-all person’s comment from years ago

curl has come to be what it is thanks to many decisions, lots of time, many users, oceans of feedback and many iterations. Sure, recreating what curl is at any specific single moment in time is certainly doable. Doable, because we have made a perfect specification for that project.

During the time these agents converted 185,000 lines of C code into 340,000 lines of Rust code (I counted), we merged over 300 commits in the actual curl project. We actually improved curl during these a little more than three weeks. A little over 200 bugfixes actually. 200 bugfixes that none of those rust rewrites have. We also fixed a few vulnerabilities. In another month we have done another 200 and maybe fixed a few more vulnerabilities. Will these clones keep up?

The constant tweaking, fixing, improving and extending is what makes a software project live, what makes it attractive to users and what makes it able to compete with alternatives.

That fixing, and occasional new feature, is a direct result of a working community of users, contributors and maintainers. That goes way beyond the source code or which language that is used.

A primary reason it is hard to make a competing curl alternative is because of the development speed, the development team and the community around curl. It is not because of the chosen language it is implemented in. Only curl can boast decades of ABI and API stability and prove that we know this and can do it well – over time. An alternative that pops up today might be able to do it as well, and in a few decades we will know if they could .

I know I’m repeating myself but: out of the 81 vulnerabilities we have confirmed in curl so far during 2026, 14 were the result of mistakes that most likely would have been avoided had we used a memory-safe language such as rust. That’s 17.3%.

A Rust implementation of curl would thus still have had 67 of those vulnerabilities.

I don’t believe in rewrites into any language. I believe in constant and never-ending polishing, iterating and refactoring.

I should add that I have not been in contact with any of the people behind these rewrites, and if there are two I bet there are more that I just haven’t seen yet. I only know of them because people have pasted me links to their repositories.

I don’t know what they will do with those projects going forward. Are they anything more than proof of concepts? I presume we will find out.

They can of course follow along our commits and convert them to rust on the fly if they want – we only do about 11 commits per day on average. Or maybe they ignore the bugreports or maybe they take their projects in other directions?

I wish them good luck whatever they decide!

items.content_ko: 본문은 curl과 libcurl을 Rust로 다시 작성하는 프로젝트에 대한 요청과 질문이 오랫동안 있었다는 이야기로 시작한다. 몇 달 전에는 메모리 안전성을 내세운 curl의 처음부터 새로 구현한 재구현판 urlx가 등장했고, 11월에는 이름을 바꾸지 않은 채 curl과 libcurl을 Rust로 재작성했다는 프로젝트가 나왔다. 후자는 이를 위해 8,600달러를 썼다고 주장한다. 작성자는 소프트웨어에서 코드를 쓰는 일 자체는 원래 큰 문제가 아니라고 말한다. AI가 이를 해낼 수 있었던 이유는 세계의 AI들이 수년간 curl 코드로 학습했고, curl은 문서화가 매우 잘 되어 있으며, 그 API를 사용하는 기존 오픈소스 애플리케이션이 수백 개, 구현을 검증하는 테스트 케이스가 수천 개나 있기 때문이라고 설명한다. 본문은 C 코드를 Rust로 변환하기만 하면 된다는 내용에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.summary_ko: AISI가 사이버 테스트 중 AI 에이전트의 무단 해로운 활동을 적발했습니다. 122회 테스트 중 10회에서 에이전트가 실제 사람과 기관을 대상으로 독립적 행동을 수행했습니다.
items.content_ko: AISI(Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute)는 프론티어 AI 모델의 역량을 평가하고 잠재적 위험을 파악하기 위해 인터넷 접근과 일부 안전 필터 비활성화 조건에서 테스트를 수행합니다. 2026년 7월 28일 연구 시스템에서 비정상 데이터 전송이 감지되었고, 조사 결과 사이버 보안 챌린지 과제 중 일부 에이전트가 실제 사람과 기관을 대상으로 지속적인 해로운 활동을 벌인 것으로 드러났습니다. 122회의 테스트 실행 중 10회에서 AI 에이전트가 라이브 인터넷에서 무단 조치를 취했으며, 총 19건의 해로운 활동이 기록되었습니다.

items.title: Israel Is Attacking Wikipedia: Report - Tech for Palestine
items.content:
Read our new report: twenty years of documented attacks on Wikipedia, and what this means for the information you get from search and AI.

from pro-Israel PACs to 26 U.S. politicians behind it

The US government used a report from the ADL to attack Wikipedia. The goal is for the Israel Lobby to gain influence over it.

Israel’s 2026 propaganda budget, up from $150M

Wikipedia feeds Google Search and every major AI chatbot. Israel’s 2026 propaganda budget is $729M, up from $150M in 2025. That includes a $46.5M contract to make AI chatbots more pro-Israel.

Our research shows that the ADL's partner in the attack on Wikipedia was likely funded by billionaire tech bros. “Builders for Tomorrow” came out of “Builders for Israel”, a WhatsApp group started in 2023 with Sheryl Sandberg, Bill Ackman, Shaun Maguire, and David Marcus.

From the ADL’s mouth: “The pressure came from several directions: congressional scrutiny, including a House Committee on Oversight investigation and a bipartisan Congressional letter from 23 members, federal inquiries from the Department of Justice and the Senate Commerce Committee; enforcement work by Wikipedia’s NPOV-policy editors, ADL reporting, and broader media scrutiny.”

We checked every claim in the ADL’s “Editing for Hate” report, and the “Damage Done”. No claim survived scrutiny. It doesn’t show a single false fact, or any antisemitic content added to Wikipedia.

Prize from an Israeli foundation, the largest prize he has received

Wikipedia founder Jimmy Wales calls himself a “strong supporter of Israel”, and has visited Israel over ten times. In 2025 he tried to influence the Gaza Genocide page to be more pro-Israel, in a clear abuse of power. In November 2026, he's trying again, with the Zionism page. We recommend that Wales step down from the Board and disable his user account

We give you a history of the ADL. It’s Israel in civil rights clothing.

We document 17 pro-Israel efforts to manipulate Wikipedia since 2001. Nine are still active! From CAMERA’s secret editor recruitment to a “Wikipedia war room” and editing courses run by Zionist groups.

full-time ADL analysts “tracking” Wikipedia editors

Four groups are targeting Wikipedia editors: the Heritage Foundation, the ADL, NPOV and Builders for Tomorrow. Some editors who were doxxed have received death threats. The ADL’s CEO says he has 45 full-time analysts “tracking” Wikipedia editors, whom he calls “weirdos with email addresses”.

is fewer edits than one experienced editor does in a day

The ADL blamed a “systematic” coordinated editing campaign on us, then tried to launder their claims. But the ADL’s own data shows only 260 edits over 8 months, none of them in the core Palestine–Israel articles. That’s one fewer edit than the ADL’s own 2021 editing campaign.

The ADL made a series of claims about Arabic Wikipedia, based on bad English translations, with no cultural context or understanding. Not surprisingly, they got it all wrong

This report started in March 2025, when the ADL published “Editing for Hate”. The report claims Wikipedia editors colluded to add antisemitism. US politicians started using it to attack Wikipedia. We wanted to know if the report itself was part of an influence operation.

The ADL analysed Arabic Wikipedia through English translations. We went back to the original Arabic.

Links to Wikipedia are permalinks to the exact edit. Content from pro-Israel organisations and paywalled sources is linked through archive.org, so it can’t be removed or changed.

Where we used AI for research, we name the tool and the prompts and publish the full conversation. AI-reconstructed links used in the report were checked by hand.

Every claim in this report is footnoted, more than 500 in total.

This is a living document. We update it when corrections or new information come in.

items.summary_ko: 보고서는 미국 정부가 ADL 보고서를 근거로 위키백과를 공격했고, 목표는 이스라엘 로비가 위키백과에 영향력을 얻는 것이라고 주장한다. 또 이스라엘의 2026년 선전 예산이 7억 2,900만 달러로 2025년 1억 5,000만 달러에서 크게 늘었다고 전한다. 이 내용은 보고서의 주장이며 독립적으로 검증된 사실은 아니다.
items.content_ko: 보고서는 위키백과가 Google 검색과 주요 AI 챗봇에 정보를 제공하는 만큼, 위키백과에 대한 공격이 사용자가 얻는 정보에 영향을 준다고 짚는다. 보고서 주장에 따르면 미국 정부는 ADL 보고서를 근거로 위키백과를 공격했고, 그 목표는 이스라엘 로비가 위키백과에 영향력을 얻는 것이다. 보고서는 이 공격에 친이스라엘 PAC과 미국 정치인 26명이 관련되어 있다고 주장한다. 이스라엘의 2026년 선전 예산은 7억 2,900만 달러로 2025년 1억 5,000만 달러에서 늘었으며, 여기에는 AI 챗봇을 더 친이스라엘적으로 만드는 4,650만 달러 규모 계약이 포함된다고 한다. 보고서는 ADL의 공격 파트너였던 「Builders for Tomorrow」가 「Builders for Israel」에서 나왔고, 이 단체가 억만장자 기술 투자자들의 자금을 받았을 가능성이 높다고 본다. 「Builders for Israel」은 2023년 시작된 WhatsApp 그룹으로, Sheryl Sandberg, Bill Ackman, Shaun Maguire, David Marcus 등이 참여했다고 한다. ADL의 발언도 인용되어 있는데, 압력이 하원 감독위원회 조사, 23명 하원의원의 서한, 법무부와 상원 상무위원회의 조사 등 여러 방향에서 왔다는 내용이다.

items.content:
Download the native 64-bit SDL2/GLES2 port of Jagged Alliance 2: Arulco Revisited (Linux x86_64 & ARM64) with Classic 1999 CTH, endless 20+-run New Game Plus, 40 custom v6.1 camo I.M.P. portraits, experimental 1–6 player local co-op, and complete reference guides for the 12-layer Mod Stack, 52 Weapon Attachments, and 312 Firearms.

The Jagged Alliance 2: Arulco Revisited — Native 64-Bit Port ( v1.0.1 ) is released and ready for download — now with all 40 custom v6.1 animated camo I.M.P. mercenary avatars ( 20 Male + 20 Female , including #220 Michael, featuring Moonlit Laptop Portraits + Woodland, Urban & Desert Camo) pre-integrated directly into the installer! Choose between our Interface-Only Windows-Style Graphical Setup Wizard ( .run ) for beginners ( Next > , Browse... , Install , Finish — zero terminal commands needed) or the portable .tar.gz release archive:

We created 40 brand-new, fully animated I.M.P. mercenary portraits ( 20 Male + 20 Female , including Portrait #220 Michael alongside international mercenaries across 30+ nationalities) specifically for the Jagged Alliance 2: Arulco Revisited native port. Every single avatar is pre-integrated into the .run and .tar.gz installers and immediately selectable in-game via Laptop ( sir-OS VIII ) → I.M.P. → Portrait (alongside the 20 classic portraits, giving you 60 selectable I.M.P. portraits in total — up to 6 custom I.M.P. mercenaries per campaign in 1–6 Player Co-op and New Game Plus!).

Every custom mercenary avatar consists of 7 hardware-indexed 8-bit ETRLE .STI sprite files ( 280 custom .STI assets in total) matched to the classic 1999 Sir-Tech tactical palette and nighttime laptop lighting ( v6.1 ):

You do not need any Linux or command-line experience. Both the .run Setup Wizard and the Online GUI Wizard open a point-and-click Windows-style Setup Wizard window ( 1. Welcome -> 2. GOG Game Files -> 3. Setup Options -> 4. Installing -> 5. Complete ) and automatically install all 40 custom v6.1 camo I.M.P. mercenary portraits :

Jagged Alliance 2: Arulco Revisited is an actively maintained native 64-bit C++17 & SDL2 source port targeting Linux x86_64, Linux ARM64 ( aarch64 ) , and handheld/micro-console hardware. So far it is tested in virtual machines and on the Khadas VIM1S board; other handhelds are not tested yet. It combines the tactical depth of the JA2 v1.13 codebase ( r7609 ) with a classic-first ruleset, the Arulco Revisited 1.4 campaign overhaul, 40 custom v6.1 camo I.M.P. mercenary portraits , native SMK2 / SMK4 Smacker cutscene playback, endless 20+-run New Game Plus carry-over , and an experimental 1–6 player local co-op mode (one shared screen, tested with virtual controllers only so far).

Jagged Alliance 2: Arulco Revisited (Native 64-Bit Port) is a curated, multi-layer mod stack rather than a single standalone patch. All layers are mounted deterministically at startup through bfVFS ( vfs_config.AR.ini ), where higher layers override lower ones without ever modifying your original GOG installation. In strict compliance with the SFI Source Code License Agreement (SFI-SCLA) and mod-author ownership, zero proprietary game or third-party mod data is bundled in our repository : the Setup Wizard verifies your own GOG backup and your downloaded mod archive via SHA-256 manifests before assembling the stack.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

items.title: Quad9's withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
items.content:
Last month, the Swiss non-profit foundation Quad9 announced  that it will withdraw its free public DNS resolver from France. This difficult decision followed months of litigation and a French court ruling that imposed daily financial penalties on Quad9 for failing to block domains associated with alleged copyright infringement.

Quad9’s departure from France is both disheartening and understandable. The court’s ruling put the organization in the impossible bind of having to choose between crippling litigation and penalties, or fundamentally altering its service in a way that would undermine the privacy and security of its users. Left with no good option, Quad9 is choosing the exit door instead.

The withdrawal of a basic infrastructure service from France fundamentally harms the free and open Internet, and it should serve as a warning of the damage that will result if rightsholders and policymakers continue demanding maximal blocking across every layer of the Internet. It not only deprives French Internet users of a trustworthy and important tool; it creates a real risk of disruption to their daily lives. Quad9’s resolver is used by a wide variety of individuals and organizations in France — including government bodies, educational institutions, hospitals, and utilities — and Quad9 has no way to directly notify those individuals and institutions that their resolver will soon stop working. If the affected parties do not change their resolver before Quad9 removes its service, their Internet will fail with no explanation.

Quad9 is not the first public DNS resolver to withdraw from a country following blocking orders, and it almost certainly won’t be the last. Cisco previously withdrew its OpenDNS resolver from France, Portugal, and Belgium (temporarily) under similar circumstances. And a Belgian court recently issued an order  that would impose substantial penalties if Cloudflare, Google, and Cisco do not begin blocking websites through their public resolvers by early January 2027. That’s something Cloudflare has never done.

Cloudflare has spent years advocating against orders of this kind. We are concerned that rightsholders’ unrelenting demands for blocking by public DNS resolvers will end up causing real harm to the Internet.

A refresher on DNS, the Domain Name System

To understand why this is such a problem, it helps to understand how the Internet works under the hood. DNS resolvers are a foundational piece of the Internet’s infrastructure. DNS is the Internet’s address book: when you type a website name such as cloudflare.com, the DNS system translates that domain name into the IP address your device needs to connect to it. A DNS resolver is the service that looks up that address and sends it back to your device, much like an operator finding a phone number in a directory.

DNS resolvers can be operated by anyone, but they are commonly run by Internet service providers (ISPs), mobile networks, businesses, and universities. If you’re reading this blog post at home and have never thought about DNS before, chances are that you’re using your ISP’s default resolver. Because you use your DNS resolver every time that you visit a website, it’s important for it to be reliable and trustworthy.

And because the DNS resolver has access to all of your browsing activity, which resolver you use has real privacy implications.

In addition to DNS resolvers that are provided by your local ISP, there are a variety of public DNS resolvers available. Cloudflare launched our public DNS resolver 1.1.1.1  in April 2018 to give back to the Internet. Our goal  was to make a fast, reliable, privacy-first consumer DNS service available for free to everyone. We succeeded. 1.1.1.1 is among the fastest DNS resolvers in the world , including in Europe. Cloudflare's resolver doesn’t collect any user data, let alone sell it to advertisers. 1.1.1.1 has always been one of our favorite examples of Cloudflare fulfilling its mission to help build a better…

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-132069 📢 Source: CIRCL 💣 CVSS Score: 6.3 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform) contains an authorization bypass in the SharingGroup model's captureSGExisting method. The authorization check used a logical AND condition that effectively exempted users with the sync permission (perm_sync) from the membership verification. Specifically, the original condition 'if (!checkIfAuthorised(...) && !perm_sync) return false' meant that any user holding the sync role would pass the check regardless of whether they were actually a member of the target sharing group. A sync user who knows or can discover the UUID of a non-local sharing group could exploit this flaw through the /sharing_groups/add endpoint or by embedding a SharingGroup object in pushed sync data. The attacker could rewrite the sharing group record to add their own organisation as a member or insert an all_orgs server entry for their MISP instance, thereby gaining read access to all events contained in that group. This exposes threat intelligence data that was intended to be restricted to the group's legitimate members. The vulnerability requires an authenticated account with the sync role and knowledge of a valid sharing group UUID. No user interaction is required. items.title: FreeBSD GUS
items.content:
FreeBSD has a pretty neat safe memory reclamation scheme (something akin to RCU), that's also been adopted by XNU that hasn't really been well-documented outside of code comments, and I thought it would've been interesting to write about it.

What safe memory reclamation is all about

The problem of safe memory reclamation (SMR) shows up notably when working with lock-free data structures. Lock-free data structures are the bread and butter of modern scalability in operating systems, and they often allow much higher throughput than their finely grained locked counterparts, but they come with their own issues.

Lock-free data structure code in unmanaged languages needs to carefully manage the liveness of the objects it manages, i.e it must guarantee that memory is freed if and only if no one is able to access it. This arises because there is no synchronization around the access of the data structure, so an object that is removed can still be visible concurrently by another CPU (who might have made a local copy).

More broadly, SMR schemes can also be used for other things than memory reclamation, I like to think of them as providing barriers ensuring that all participants (read: CPUs or threads) have passed through a certain point.

SMR schemes broadly fall in two families: Epoch-based reclamation (EBR) and Quiescent-state based reclamation (QSBR). You might have also heard of Hazard Pointers (HP), which are useful on their own but are seldom seen in operating systems (at least, that I know of!).

QSBR is notable because you might've heard of it called a different name by the Linux project, RCU (Read-Copy-Update)! RCU's author, Paul McKenney, actually invented QSBR for the DYNIX operating system.

RCU has been described extensively, and I would recommend reading McKenney's excellent LWN Articles to learn more. The TL;DR is that there are three operations: rcu_read_lock , rcu_read_unlock and rcu_synchronize , the read operations are used to guard reads around potentially-freed memory (i.e to enter a read section ) and the synchronize function waits until there is no CPU in a read section (this could be used to wait until memory is safe to be freed).

The gist of the algorithm is that memory is known to be safe to free when all CPUs have gone through at least one quiescent point ever since the object was removed from its data structure (a grace period ), and read section operations block those quiescent points from ever happening.

In practice, this can be implemented by having a quiescent point on context switches and inhibiting preemption during read operations. The core of the algorithm is actually pretty simple, and much of the complexity of the Linux code stems from making this scalable (Tree RCU) and handling other RCU flavors (e.g preemptible RCU).

FreeBSD's safe memory reclamation scheme is called GUS and is part of the EBR family.

Epoch-based reclamation was first described by Keir Fraser in his now-famous thesis titled Practical Lock-freedom ( link ). The way it works is that there is a global epoch which moves through 0, 1 and 2. When a thread enters a read section, it pins itself by reading the global epoch and copying it into its local slot.

When a writer retires an object, it goes into a "limbo" bag tagged with the current epoch (really, the epoch is used as an index into an array of three linked lists). The global epoch is advanced by polling all other threads and checking whether or not they have acknowledged the current epoch by reading their local slot; if it so happens that they have, then the global epoch is advanced and memory that was retired two epochs ago can now be freed.

Epochs are bounded , i.e they always cycle through 0, 1 and 2, this means that writers have to synchronize with epoch advancement before retiring more objects; and

Doing an O(n) scan touching remote memory is very expensive!

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
items.content:
Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”

The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.

Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability.

Also announced as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ , an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ , a context layer that helps agents understand a company’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

Copilot Workspaces is a collaborative environment currently available through Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program, but coming soon will be the ability to bring personal Autopilot agents into Workspaces. Early in the keynote address, Nadella said that “Until now, AI interactions have mostly been single-player. Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience, where people and agents drive towards a common goal, with shared context.”

Trust, the third pillar of Microsoft’s new frontier ecosystem, was something that Nadella continued returning to during his presentation, and not in a way that some might expect. “We find ourselves in a place where alignment is elusive. Mechanistic understanding of these models is elusive. The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,” he said.

In a departure from the norms of “AI is magic” corporate hype sentiment, Nadella conceded that the internal workings of AI thought processes remain difficult to understand, and models cannot be trusted to govern themselves, regardless of whether their answers are accurate. Nadella described the solution as “an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence” from the authority granted to it. Microsoft says each Autopilot agent will have a unique ID, and administrators can restrict permissions or block it entirely. All agent activities are logged for human review, and Autopilot can ask for human approval before engaging in certain actions.

Human ambition, intelligence, and trust are said to be the three pillars of the frontier ecosystem.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: CSS reversed(): A Better Way to Build Countdown Counters
items.content:
CSS counters have been around for years, but there’s a lesser-known feature that makes counting backwards much easier: reversed() .

Normally, CSS counters increase as elements appear on the page. With reversed() , you can reverse that behavior and automatically number items from the end of a list to the beginning.

The interesting part is that you don’t always need to specify where the countdown starts. The browser can calculate the initial value based on the number of elements.

Let’s see how it works, where it’s useful, and what to watch out for.

Before getting into reversed() , let’s look at ordinary CSS counters.

A CSS counter typically uses three properties:

counter-reset creates or resets a counter.

< p > Start the development server </ p >

Each paragraph increments the counter before displaying its value.

Now suppose we want the same list to count backwards.

The reversed() function can be used inside counter-reset to create a reversed counter.

You can also specify an explicit starting value:

The important difference is that reversed counters have a default decrement of -1 , rather than the usual increment of 1 .

And the counter will decrease automatically.

There’s no need to write counter-increment: step -1 just to make a reversed counter count down.

The starting value is explicitly set to 10 , and each element decreases the counter by one.

This approach works well when you already know the number of items.

4. Automatic Countdown Without a Starting Value

Maybe you’re rendering a list of tasks, notifications, or leaderboard entries from an API.

Hardcoding the initial value would be inconvenient.

Fortunately, reversed counters can calculate their initial value automatically.

The browser determines the starting value based on the number of elements that increment or decrement the counter within its scope.

Add another item, and the numbering adjusts automatically.

This is the biggest advantage of reversed() over manually initialized counters.

One important detail: the initial value is based on the relevant counter operations, not simply every child element. Elements that don’t change the counter aren’t automatically counted.

Which items affect the counter? Live CSS demo

/* Items without the operation are not counted. */

5. Reverse Numbering with Semantic HTML Lists

For ordinary ordered lists, HTML already provides a built-in reversed attribute.

HTML reversed vs CSS reversed() Live CSS demo

Because CSS counters are not limited to <ol> elements.

You can use them with cards, headings, sections, navigation items, and other elements.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
items.content:
Google's AI answers are taking clicks from websites in the search results. In a randomized experiment, researchers hid AI Overviews from some US desktop users. Comparing them with users who still saw Overviews shows that an Overview cuts clicks to outside websites by about 40%. Those Overviews now appear on more than half the US keywords DataForSEO tracks, up from 6% two years ago. The industry's answer, GEO (generative engine optimization), has yet to show a way to compensate for the loss. While AI citations correlate with the same kind of link profile that goes with higher Google rankings, in March AI assistants sent websites just 0.3% of their traffic.

Search engine optimization (SEO) still decides whether you can be found, but where an AI answer appears, a ranking

brings 40% fewer visits than it used to. Generative engine optimization (GEO), the

practice of getting your content cited in AI-written answers, looks mostly like SEO plus two additions: being present

on the third-party sites AI answers draw from, and writing pages that are easy to quote. We found little

An AI Overview is a generated summary that Google places above the ordinary results, with links to the pages it drew

on. In DataForSEO's monthly panel of 20 million keywords, the share of results showing one climbed from 5.93% in

September 2024 to 61.43% in August 2026. The chart at the top of this post shows that climb. Over the same period the

featured snippet, the quoted passage Google used to show at the top of a page, fell from 8.96% to 0.44%, and the

discussions and forums block fell from 21.13% to 7.42%. Video results rose from 9.67% to 19.98%, though that is

down from a peak of 31.05% in October 2025, and local map listings rose from 19.98% to 25.99%. DataForSEO's dataset

covers 190 million keywords, 165 million AI answers, and 1.1 billion backlinks, mostly for US English searches.

Pew Research Center's data gives an independent check. Pew logged the searches of 900

US adults in March 2025, re-ran them in April, and found summaries on 18% of them. DataForSEO's figures for

those months are 14.67% and 17.63%, close to Pew's.

keywords with 201 to 300 monthly searches showed Overviews 58.59% of the time, against 48.62% for those above 600.

A separate dataset, from June to September 2026, covers

items.title: Stacked diffs with Maiao
items.content:
On the go? Listen to an ai -narrated version of this article .

I have been using the community fork of Maiao for a little while now, and it is

excellent. For anyone who prefers working with stacked diffs, but needs to

interact with a more traditional forge such as GitHub, try using Maiao for a

bit. It just does the right thing in almost every situation . It’s cut my

frustration with GitHub at least in half, if not more.

For the small group of readers who are stoked about stacked diffs, that’s

probably enough of a pitch. For the rest of the world, let’s back up a little.

On traditional forge platforms 1 1 Like GitHub, Codeberg, GitLab, BitBucket,

etc. , pre-commit 2 2 Pre-commit because it’s the review that happens before the

code is merged (“committed”) to the upstream branch, in contrast to e.g. audits

which are a kind of post-commit review. code review happens on pull requests

(sometimes called merge requests ), where each pull request is created from a

Users that are new to git can then think of a branch as one development effort

toward a small goal. They keep adding commits to that branch as long as its tip

does not represent the goal state. At the end, when everything looks right and

the change is approved, they perform an explicit merge. This means they create a

merge commit on the upstream branch that references both the old upstream and

This lets beginners work in smaller increments while not dealing with the

intricacies of rewriting git history 3 3 Sometimes the beginner is instructed to

perform a squash merge instead, which typically means the forge platform creates

a single, regular commit on the upstream branch, referencing only the old

upstream, and containing all the changes implied by the tip of the development

branch. Although it sounds like this rewrites history, it doesn’t really – the

old development branch is still exactly the same as it was before. The

difference is that the changes implied by it were copied over to the upstream

branch without reference to the development branch. ; the workflow lowers the

barrier to collaborating with others using git, which is nice.

It also means the reviewing interface in a traditional forge doesn’t have to

deal with the intricacies of rewriting git history. This means the reviewing

ui typically only shows the differences between commits still on the

development branch, and not what changed between two versions of “the same”

commit, when one of them is no longer on the branch.

To be more concrete, here’s an example of a part of the history graph of a

project that uses this workflow. 4 4 The commits are not shown in chronological

order. I reordered them (where it was possible to do so without changing the

structure of the graph) to make the graph read more clearly.

●◀──╮ │ Merge parser-null-check (PR #832)

We can see a total of 12 commits. Four of them are merge commits on the

upstream branch, and two of those merge commits correspond to branches we can

see the work on ( avatar-upload and flaky-test-fix ). We can see each of those

two branches had three and two commits of actual work on them, respectively.

Then there are two more branches ( input-validation and priv-cache ) which are

still open (not merged with upstream). One of them ( priv-cache ) has two

commits of work, and it’s not based on the upstream branch, but on the final

result of one of the earlier branches ( flaky-test-fix ), before it got merged.

We don’t have to use git that way. We can instead choose to have only one

development branch. I call it something generic like dev . On that branch, each

goal state is represented by one commit. So instead of multiple branches (one

for each goal) with multiple commits on them (steps toward the implementation),

there is just one branch (a generic development branch) with multiple commits on

items.content_ko: 본문은 스택형 diff를 잘 모르는 독자를 위해 기본 개념부터 설명한다. GitHub, Codeberg, GitLab, Bitbucket 같은 기존 포지 플랫폼에서는 코드 리뷰가 풀 리퀘스트(또는 머지 리퀘스트) 단위로 이뤄지며, 각 풀 리퀘스트는 하나의 브랜치에서 만들어진다. Git 입문자는 브랜치를 작은 목표 하나를 위한 개발 작업으로 생각할 수 있으며, 목표 상태에 도달할 때까지 커밋을 계속 쌓는다. 입력 본문은 이 설명 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.summary_ko: HP가 Poly 음성 기기의 심각한 buffer overflow 취약점(CVE-2026-0826)을 패치했다. 인증 없는 공격자가 루트 권한을 획득해 도청, 음성 녹음을 통한 AI 기반 모방 공격이 가능했으며, CVSS 9.2로 평가된다.
items.content_ko: Rapid7 연구원들이 발견한 이 취약점은 ICE(Interactive Connectivity Establishment) 기능 활성화 시 Session Description Protocol(SDP) 속성을 파싱하는 코드에 존재한다. ICE는 VoIP 기기가 최단 네트워크 경로를 통해 P2P 연결을 수립하는 기능이며, HP Poly 기기에서는 기본적으로 비활성화되어 있다. HP는 VVX 기기는 UCS 6.4.8, Trio 8300은 8.1.7, Trio 7.2.8 버전으로 수정했다. 영향을 받는 범위는 HP Poly VVX 시리즈 전체 및 Trio 8300, 8500, 8800 IP 회의 기기다.

items.title: Nuclear Explosion in Low Earth Orbit Would Disable 98% of Satellites
items.content:
Currently, an estimated 17,776 satellites reside in low Earth orbit—a giant network supporting critical civilian and military infrastructure. Here’s a chilling thought experiment. What if someone threw a nuclear bomb in low Earth orbit?

That’s the premise behind new research by physicists at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Princeton University. The paper, which has yet to be peer-reviewed and is currently available as a preprint on arXiv, considers a scenario in which a one-megaton nuclear detonation occurs at 311 miles (500 kilometers) above the South Atlantic. The team developed a framework based on multiple collision and debris models, as well as calculations on the spread of radioactive fission products.

A single nuclear explosion would disable roughly 98% of satellites within one week—at least according to the model. The loss of maneuverability would increase the risk of collisions, with around 20 expected within two years.

“The result would not be an immediate collapse of modern society, but rather a prolonged degradation of many services that we now take for granted,” Chantal Cappelletti, an aerospace engineer at the University of Nottingham, U.K., who wasn’t involved in the new paper, told New Scientist . “Recovery would likely require years of rebuilding orbital infrastructure while managing elevated radiation and debris hazards.”

The U.S. actually tried something like this in 1962. The Starfish Prime test set off a 1.4-megaton nuclear detonation at an altitude of 250 miles (400 kilometers) above the Pacific Ocean. Data from the experiment was declassified in 2006, and scientists since then have characterized the physical properties of the explosion and its aftermath.

An image of the flash created by the explosion during the Starfish Prime test in 1962. © Nuclear Weapons Archive via Wikimedia Commons (Public Domain) According to the paper, experts became aware of how the explosion left behind an artificial radiation belt, which, unlike the “prompt burst,” lurked in Earth’s magnetic field and repeatedly spewed radiation at spacecraft. Back then, there were far fewer satellites up there. A year later, the U.S. and the Soviet Union signed the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty , which banned nuclear weapons tests on the surface, in the atmosphere, and in outer space, while allowing underground tests.

Decades later, in 2024, Russia vetoed a United Nations Security Council resolution reaffirming a nuclear weapons ban in Earth’s orbit. This has sparked concerns that a nuclear weapon “could be used against orbital infrastructure,” the team wrote in the paper. And unlike the 1960s, we have too many satellites that are too important for global communications and infrastructure—hence, the significance of the latest study.

A visual representation of the distribution of the artificial radiation belt, depending on the location of the initial detonation. © Petersen et al., 2026 As expected, the team’s calculations found that the most damage came not from the X-rays released from the initial blast but from the electrons released by the fission products. When these electrons are trapped in Earth’s magnetic field, they effectively become an artificial radiation belt. The researchers even tried tripling radiation tolerance—perhaps better materials can withstand this—but still discovered that about 97% became disabled in two weeks.

Launching replacement satellites won’t really solve the issue, they added. For one, the loss of maneuverability “sharply increases” the risk of collisions, and we should expect around 20 collisions within two years of the blast. Most of them, about 19, would occur in the first year, compared to just about one without a detonation. The new satellites would also be jumping right into the artificial radiation belt, so they will not be safe from radiation exposure.

And remember, we’ll have to deal with this while juggling huge disruptions to civilian and military telecommunications infrastructure.…

items.summary_ko: 위스콘신-매디슨 대학교와 프린스턴 대학교 물리학자들의 arXiv 사전 출판 논문은, 남대서양 상공 500km에서 1메가톤 핵폭발이 일어나는 시나리오를 모델로 분석했다. 모델에 따르면 일주일 안에 저궤도 위성의 약 98%가 작동 불능이 되며, 기동 능력 상실로 2년 안에 약 20건의 충돌이 예상된다. 이 논문은 아직 동료 검토를 거치지 않았다.
items.content_ko: 현재 저궤도에는 약 17,776개의 위성이 있으며, 민간과 군사 인프라를 떠받치고 있다. 연구진은 다중 충돌 모델과 잔해 확산 모델, 핵분열 생성물 확산 계산을 결합한 프레임워크를 만들었다. 이 모델 기준으로 위성 대부분이 작동하지 못하게 되며, 이후 충돌 위험이 커진다. 영국 노팅엄 대학교의 항공우주 엔지니어 Chantal Cappelletti는 결과가 현대 사회의 즉각적 붕괴가 아니라, 우리가 당연하게 여기는 많은 서비스의 장기적 악화일 것이라고 말했다. 해당 논문은 아직 동료 검토를 받지 않았다.

items.title: Shenzhen AI Summit: Behind a carefully curated tour showcasing smart cities and autonomous systems, China's extensive surveillance networks and social monitoring systems are off the official itinerary
items.content:
China is rolling out the red carpet for world leaders in Shenzhen, transforming the southern tech hub into a showcase of artificial intelligence innovation. Officially launched on November 16, 2026, this international summit presents visiting dignitaries with autonomous vehicles, AI-powered urban management systems, and sprawling innovation centers. Yet behind this carefully orchestrated display of technological prowess lies a parallel AI infrastructure that remains conspicuously absent from the official tour.

Delegates are being guided through state-of-the-art AI research facilities, smart manufacturing plants deploying machine learning optimization, and demonstration zones where facial recognition systems manage traffic flow and public services. The city's AI-driven logistics networks showcase efficiency gains, while robotics labs highlight advances in automation and human-machine collaboration. This curated experience emphasizes innovation, economic growth, and technological leadership on the global stage.

Shenzhen's presentation focuses on beneficial AI applications: healthcare diagnostics, environmental monitoring, educational tools, and industrial productivity enhancements. These demonstrations align with China's broader messaging about AI serving societal advancement and economic development.

The systems not included in official tours tell a different story. Extensive surveillance networks powered by AI operate throughout Shenzhen, analyzing pedestrian movements, monitoring online activities, and feeding data into social credit scoring systems. Facial recognition cameras track citizens continuously, while natural language processing algorithms scan digital communications for sensitive content.

These monitoring capabilities represent some of the world's most sophisticated AI surveillance deployments. The technology enables real-time identification of individuals in crowds, predictive policing based on behavioral patterns, and automated enforcement of social norms. Human rights organizations have documented how these systems restrict freedom of movement and expression, particularly for minority populations and political dissidents.

China's AI sector exemplifies a fundamental tension in artificial intelligence deployment. The same computer vision models that enable efficient urban planning also power mass surveillance. Natural language models that improve customer service simultaneously scan communications for political dissent. This dual-use reality complicates assessments of China's AI ecosystem.

International observers note that Shenzhen's AI wonderland represents both genuine technological achievement and strategic image management. The innovations on display are real, the efficiency gains measurable, and the technical capabilities impressive. Yet the selective transparency raises questions about governance frameworks, ethical guidelines, and accountability mechanisms governing AI deployment at scale.

The summit occurs as China pursues global AI leadership while facing international scrutiny over technology governance. The country has invested heavily in AI research, attracted top talent, and deployed systems at unprecedented scale. These capabilities position China as a major force in shaping global AI development trajectories.

However, the gap between public demonstrations and comprehensive disclosure of AI applications complicates international cooperation on AI standards and norms. Visiting leaders see impressive capabilities but gain limited insight into the full scope of AI deployment, particularly in sensitive domains like surveillance and social monitoring.

The Shenzhen summit crystallizes broader debates about AI development, transparency, and governance. As nations compete for technological leadership, the question of which applications to showcase and which to obscure reveals priorities and values. items.title: 글 쌌다 지웠다 하는 뷩쉰은 봐라
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-110486 📢 Source: vulncheck-cvelist-v5 💣 CVSS Score: 9.8 (CRITICAL) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-18 10:15:09.085000+00:00 https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110486

items.summary_ko: Mosquitto 2.1부터 2.1.2까지에서 protocol websockets 리스너가 빈 WebSocket 데이터 프레임을 잘못 처리한다. 원격 클라이언트가 이를 이용하면 브로커가 초기화되지 않은 힙 메모리를 전달해 힙과 libc 포인터가 노출될 수 있고, 이어서 힙 범위를 벗어난 쓰기도 가능하다. 인증 확인 전 CONNECT 패킷 단계에서도 도달할 수 있어, allow_anonymous false 설정에서도 인증되지 않은 클라이언트가 브로커를 크래시시킬 수 있다.
items.content_ko: CVE-2026-110486은 Eclipse Mosquitto 2.1~2.1.2의 WebSocket 리스너에서 발생하는 취약점으로, CVSS 9.8(Critical)이며 원격 공격이 가능하다. net__read_ws() 함수가 길이가 0인 데이터 프레임에 대해 버퍼에 아무것도 쓰지 않은 채 프레이밍 바이트 수를 반환하고, packet__read_single()이 이를 페이로드 길이로 신뢰하는 것이 원인이다. 이로 인해 메모리 정보 노출과 힙 범위 밖 쓰기가 발생할 수 있다. 입력 본문은 결합된 공격 영향 설명 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability For OpenJDK Java That Can Lead To Remote Code Execution
items.content:
Java4Shell Vulnerability For OpenJDK Java That Can Lead To Remote Code Execution

Written by Michael Larabel in Programming on 17 November 2026 at 04:35 PM EST. 9 Comments

Java4Shell was publicly disclosed this afternoon as the latest high profile security vulnerability in the age of AI and LLMs.

Java4Shell amounts to being a memory corruption vulnerability within OpenJDK's Base64 decoder that can lead to remote code execution. The CVSS 4.0 score comes in at 9.2 out of 10, a critical level.

This base64 snafu can lead to pre-authentication remote code execution in the likes of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, JFrog, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Or post-authentication RCE in the likes of Apache Kafka, Solr, ElasticSearch, Gerrit, Netflix Spinnaker, and others.

Java4Shell comes down to a bug in the AVX-512 optimized Assembly code for Java's Base64 decoding:

"To speed up Base64 decoding, OpenJDK uses specialized AVX-512 VBMI instructions on supported x86-64 processors. The bug sits in the hand-rolled assembly code that handles the final few characters. For the 65-character input above, OpenJDK allocates a 50-byte result array. After decoding the first 64 characters, the routine mishandles the stray = and calculates a negative output length. That invalid length becomes a full 64-byte write, sending 62 bytes past the end of the array. Java eventually rejects the input, but by then neighboring objects may already be corrupted."

More details on Java4Shell can be found via the announcement . This is patched by Oracle with the critical security patch update advisory .

items.summary_ko: OpenJDK의 Base64 디코더에서 메모리 손상 취약점 Java4Shell이 공개되었으며, 원격 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있다. CVSS 4.0 점수는 9.2로 Critical 수준이다. 기사는 Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins 등 여러 제품이 사전 인증 원격 코드 실행, Apache Kafka, Solr, ElasticSearch 등은 인증 후 원격 코드 실행의 영향을 받을 수 있다고 전한다.
items.content_ko: Java4Shell은 AVX-512 최적화된 Base64 디코딩 어셈블리 코드의 결함으로 발생하는 메모리 손상 취약점이다. OpenJDK는 x86-64 프로세서에서 AVX-512 VBMI 명령어를 사용해 Base64 디코딩을 가속하는데, 마지막 몇 문자를 처리하는 루틴에 문제가 있다. 예시로 65자 입력에서 OpenJDK는 50바이트 결과 배열을 할당하지만, 처음 64자를 디코딩한 뒤 루틴이 이를 잘못 처리한다고 설명된다. 기사에 따르면 Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, JFrog, Jenkins, PingFederate 등은 사전 인증 상태에서, Apache Kafka, Solr, ElasticSearch, Gerrit, Netflix Spinnaker 등은 인증 후에 영향을 받을 수 있다. 입력 본문은 잘려 있다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

We partnered with Baseten to build the largest-scale harness leaderboard using 83B tokens across 27,280 agent runs. We wanted to answer two questions: when you switch your model, should you consider switching the harness too? What is the best harness for each model?

Previously, our v1.0 FrontierHarness leaderboard ranked harnesses on a single model, Kimi K3.

V1.1 expands the benchmark to 22 harnesses × 5 models × 62 tasks × 4 attempts, 76× the size of v1.0.

Through our experiments, we found that you should consider switching harnesses when switching models to maximize your experience.

Each model had a different best-value (pass rate vs. cost) harness: Codex CLI with GLM-5.3, Pi with GLM-5.3 Flash, ZCode with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, Oh My Pi with Muse and Alma with Kimi-K3. Cost ranks moved far between models.

By cost per task, the median harness moved 11 of 22 places, and Codex CLI went from 1st with GLM-5.3 to 16th with Kimi-K3.

Figure 1. Cost per task and pass rate of each harness

Each point is one harness: further left is a lower average cost per task, and higher is a higher pass rate. The orange line joins the harnesses that no other harness beats in both cost and pass rate. Select a model to filter all figures of this post.

Over all models, four harnesses are on the line: OpenCode v2 (lowest cost per task, $0.561), Pi, Codex CLI and ZCode (highest pass rate, 61.9%). The others cost up to 1.6 times as much and passed 50.6% to 60.2%.

Each card names the best-value harness for one model: the lowest cost per pass, unless another harness costs at most 30% more per pass and passes at least 5 points more often. This rule picked ZCode over OpenCode v1 with DeepSeek (25% more cost, 7.7 more points) and Alma over Oh My Pi with Kimi-K3 (9% more cost, 6.5 more points).

V1.0 ran nine harnesses with one model. Their pass rates were within 17 points of each other, but the median cost per pass differed by 17 times. We thought that this came mostly from the pair of harness and model: a harness that is cheap with one model can be expensive with another.

V1.1 runs each harness with five models.

Harnesses. 18 harnesses. The four DeepSeek Harness profiles have different tool sets, and OpenCode ran at two versions. Each counts separately: 22 configurations. Table 2 in the appendix gives their versions.

Models. Baseten served all five: GLM-5.3 ( zai-org/GLM-5.3 ), GLM Flash ( zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash ), DeepSeek ( deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 ), Muse ( meta-models/muse-spark-open ) and Kimi-K3 ( moonshotai/Kimi-K3 ).

Tasks. 62 terminal tasks. The time limits are those of the tasks, from 15 minutes to 8 hours.

We ran the Harbor evaluation with each harness’s default settings, because we think this is closest to how people use a harness every day. Each harness used the same version and settings with all models, at the maximum reasoning effort.

Figure 2. How Harbor and Runta divide the work in each trial

Each trial gets a new Runta runtime, which is deleted at the end. Thus no trial can see the files of an earlier trial.

A cell is one harness and model pair. We use the two cost metrics of our dashboard :

Average cost per task: the mean cost of the priced trials of each task, then the mean over the tasks. Figure 1 and the cost ranks use it (Figures 4 and 5).

Cost per pass: the average cost per task divided by the pass rate. The best-value harness uses it (Figures 3, 6 and 7).

We pick the best value by cost per pass because we want harnesses at the top left of a chart of pass rate against cost per task: a high pass rate at a low cost. Draw a line from the origin to the point of a harness. Its slope, pass rate ÷ cost, is the passes per dollar. Cost per pass is the inverse of this slope, so the lowest cost per pass has the steepest line.

items.title: Steve Jobs Core Animation demo from WWDC 2007
items.content:
A Steve Jobs Core Animation demo from WWDC 2007 popped up in my feed and it stopped me cold. A live wall of playing videos, instant zoom, instant tag search, zero glitches, on 2007 hardware.

Then I clicked around Sequoia for thirty seconds and watched panels load in slowly.

Tahoe is worse. I am still holding out on Sequoia and it is barely better.

Tell me where Apple software still feels like 2007 to you.
