items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

A scheduled nationwide emergency alert test will interrupt television and radio programming Tuesday afternoon.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will conduct a test on Tuesday to evaluate the effectiveness of the Emergency Alert System.

This test is performed at least once every three years, as federal law requires. It allows officials to identify any technical or operational problems before the system is needed in an actual emergency.

Unlike the last nationwide test in October 2023, this test will not include Wireless Emergency Alerts. That means cellphones will not receive the emergency alert.

When will the emergency alert test happen?

The test is scheduled to begin at 2:20 p.m. eastern time on Tuesday, Nov. 17.

The alert will be distributed across the country at the following times:

The alert is expected to interrupt television, radio, cable, and satellite video programs for about one minute.

According to FEMA and the FCC, viewers and listeners will hear the following message:

"This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, covering the United States from 2:20 to 2:50 hours ET. This is only a test. No action is required by the public."

Normal programming will resume after the approximate one-minute message.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: AI is killing All About Berlin
items.content:
This is the traffic to All About Berlin , the website that I run since 2017, and live from since 2020. After 7 years of growth, it has lost 70% 75% of its traffic to Google AI Overviews.

When you Googled something, you used to get a link to my website. Now you get a page of ads, then an AI-generated answer trained on my content, then finally a link to my website. This has a devastating impact on traffic.

It’s hard to fund my work with only a quarter of my audience. Soon, I will need another way to pay my rent. Instead of writing new guides, I already spend my days preparing for that future.

It’s not just about the money. I have poured 8 years of my life into making something good and useful. Strangers’ faces light up when they learn that I run All About Berlin. Local and federal government offices refer people to my guides. The Berlin immigration office uses my data about themselves . It inspired two government portals and a few similar websites in other cities.

If my work just get mixed into an AI-generated answer, I lose my voice and my audience. My carefully chosen words lose their meaning. No one shakes my hand and buys me a beer. No one tells me how their citizenship application went.

This is not an isolated case. Many website owners have reached out in private to commiserate. Some have paywalled their work. Others have given up and moved on. They keep the websites online, but they no longer update them. It’s just not worth it.

It will get worse. Last week, Google has made two announcements: AI-generated answers will replace search results entirely, and they have ads in them. 1 This is the future of the internet. No websites, just a chat box with ads.

I don’t know where All About Berlin fits in that future.

This was also discussed on Mastodon , Hacker News , LinkedIn and Twitter . If you are affected, reach out . Let me know how you are doing. You are not going through this alone.

items.title_ko: AI 요약이 베를린 정보 사이트 All About Berlin의 트래픽을 잠식하고 있다
items.summary_ko: 2017년부터 운영해 온 베를린 정보 사이트 All About Berlin은 7년간 성장한 뒤 Google AI Overviews로 인해 트래픽의 약 70~75%를 잃었다고 운영자는 밝혔다. 검색 결과에서 사이트 링크가 AI가 생성한 답변 뒤로 밀려나면서 수익과 운영 지속이 어려워졌다고 한다. 운영자는 콘텐츠가 AI 답변에 흡수되면 자신의 목소리와 독자가 사라질 수 있다고 우려한다.
items.content_ko: 운영자는 2017년부터 All About Berlin을 운영했고 2020년부터 베를린에 거주하며 사이트를 운영하고 있다. 7년간 성장했던 트래픽이 Google AI Overviews 때문에 약 70~75% 줄었다고 한다. 과거에는 검색하면 사이트 링크가 바로 나왔지만, 지금은 광고, AI가 자신의 콘텐츠를 학습해 만든 답변, 그 다음에야 링크가 나온다. 독자가 4분의 1만 남아 작업 자금을 마련하기 어렵고, 머지않아 생활비를 충당할 다른 방법을 찾아야 할 것 같다고 밝혔다. 그는 새 가이드를 쓰는 대신 그 준비에 시간을 쓰고 있다. 지방 및 연방 정부 기관이 사이트의 가이드를 안내하고, 베를린 이민국은 자신들과 관련된 데이터를 사이트에서 가져다 쓰며, 이 사이트가 정부 포털 두 곳과 다른 도시의 유사 사이트에도 영감을 주었다고 한다. 글은 AI 답변에 작성 내용이 섞이면 목소리와 의미가 사라진다는 우려로 이어지며 중간에 끝난다.

items.title: Redict is deprecated
items.content:
I must unfortunately announce that Redict is officially deprecated, and Redict

I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to

protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose.

However, with the valkey project’s success, and Redis’s return to a copyleft

license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community.

We recommend that Redict users switch to valkey , which

uses a permissive license but has better long-term prospects. We advise against

switching back to Redis; though it is once again open source, and copyleft, it

uses a contributor license agreement which will facilitate another rug-pull when

Switching to valkey is straightforward: if you install from your package

manager, simply install valkey and move your config file:

If you use containers, simply pull the valkey container instead and ensure that

it runs with the appropriate config file.

Thanks to everyone who has contributed to Redict, endorsed the fork as the

future of Redis, and switched to it on their own machines. We had a good run :)
items.title_ko: Redict, 공식 중단 발표
items.summary_ko: Redict 프로젝트가 공식적으로 중단되었다. Redis 사용자들을 카피레프트(copyleft) 라이선스 아래 결집하려던 목표였으나, valkey의 성공과 Redis의 카피레프트 라이선스 복귀 이후 지속 가능한 커뮤니티를 만들지 못했다. 사용자는 valkey로 옮길 것을 권장하며, 패키지 관리자 설치나 컨테이너 기준으로 전환은 간단하다고 설명한다.
items.content_ko: Redict 프로젝트는 공식적으로 중단(deprecated)되었다고 발표되었다. 이 프로젝트는 Redis 사용자들을 카피레프트 라이선스 아래 모아, 향후 러그풀(rug-pull)로부터 스스로를 보호하려는 목적으로 만들어졌다. 그러나 valkey 프로젝트가 성공을 거두었고 Redis가 다시 카피레프트 라이선스로 돌아오면서, Redict는 지속 가능한 커뮤니티를 만들지 못했다. 이에 Redict 사용자에게는 퍼미시브(permissive) 라이선스를 쓰지만 장기 전망이 더 나은 valkey로 옮길 것이 권장된다. Redis로 되돌아가는 것은 권장하지 않는데, Redis는 다시 오픈소스이자 카피레프트가 되었지만 기여자 라이선스 계약(CLA)을 사용하고 있어 향후 또 다른 러그풀이 가능하다는 이유다. 패키지 관리자로 설치했다면 valkey를 설치하고 설정 파일을 옮기면 되고, 컨테이너를 쓴다면 valkey 컨테이너를 받아 적절한 설정 파일로 실행하면 된다. 끝으로 Redict에 기여하고 이 포크를 Redis의 미래로 지지해 준 사람들에게 감사를 전한다.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

items.title: State of HTML 2026
items.content:
For what seemed like eons, it felt like the web was standing still. Web APIs were limited compared to their native equivalents. Building anything more complex that a single-column layout required lots of hacks, duct tape, and swearing.

As a result, JavaScript came in to fill the void, and we witnessed a literal explosion of frameworks, libraries, and everything in-between.

But these days, things have flipped. JavaScript frameworks have consolidated around a couple solid options, and the pace of change has slowed down. Meanwhile, browser vendors have finally gotten their act together and are now working hand-in-hand to release new features faster than ever before–and ensure they work across the board!

And this is happening just in time for the widespread adoption of AI-assisted code generation, which has no qualms about skipping JavaScript frameworks altogether and leveraging browser APIs directly when it makes sense.

So this feels like the perfect time to go back to basics and brush up on what modern browsers can actually do. And this survey is here to help!

Leave us your email and we’ll let you know when the next survey takes place.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-112213 📢 Source: INCIBE 💣 CVSS Score: 6.9 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the pixReadMemJp2kCore() function in Leptonica, located in jp2kio.c. The function retrieves the output dimensions only for component 0 and uses a common index to iterate through the buffers of all components. If the remaining components have smaller dimensions, the traversal exceeds the bounds of their sample buffers, which are allocated by OpenJPEG. When processing a specially crafted JPEG 2000 image, data read from adjacent dynamic memory may be incorporated into the pixels of the decoded image and result in information disclosure to anyone who can access the output. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-18T09:58:14.836Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112213
items.title_ko: Leptonica JPEG 2000 디코더의 경계 초과 읽기 취약점(CVE-2026-112213)
items.summary_ko: Leptonica의 jp2kio.c에 있는 pixReadMemJp2kCore() 함수에서 경계 초과 읽기 취약점이 보고되었다. 구성 요소 0의 크기만 기준으로 모든 버퍼를 순회해, 나머지 구성 요소의 크기가 더 작으면 OpenJPEG가 할당한 샘플 버퍼 범위를 넘어선다. 특수하게 조작된 JPEG 2000 이미지를 처리하면 인접한 동적 메모리의 데이터가 디코딩된 이미지 픽셀에 섞여 정보가 노출될 수 있으며, CVSS 점수는 6.9(MEDIUM)이고 원격 악용이 가능하다고 표시되어 있다.
items.content_ko: Leptonica의 jp2kio.c 파일 내 pixReadMemJp2kCore() 함수는 출력 크기를 구성 요소 0에서만 가져오고, 공통 인덱스로 모든 구성 요소의 버퍼를 순회한다. 나머지 구성 요소의 크기가 더 작으면 OpenJPEG가 할당한 샘플 버퍼 범위를 벗어나 읽게 된다. 특수하게 만든 JPEG 2000 이미지를 처리하면 인접한 동적 메모리 데이터가 디코딩된 이미지 픽셀에 포함되어, 출력에 접근할 수 있는 누구에게나 정보가 노출될 수 있다. 공개일은 2026-11-18이다.

items.title: Github Redesign (2019)
items.content:
Github design is pretty good: it gets the job done, it’s clean, has consistent visual language, its design is calm and suitable for everyday use.

Given all that, there are still many areas that could be improved. Today we’ll take one interface—repository page—and look what UI problems it has and if we can fix them.

Let’s start with the biggest issue right away: information architecture. Take tabs. Currently there’re two levels of tabs, one nested under the other:

If you are a programmer, you might be surprised but other people normally don’t like hierarchies. Nested structures are hard to grasp, remember, navigate, and grouping is very often non-intuitive. Nested tabs are one of the worst UI patterns out there.

Then there’s a plain usability issue: let’s say I’m in Wiki and need to see Releases. What should I do? There’s no Releases tab visible, so I must figure out somehow that Releases are part of the Code (?). That makes almost no sense. Releases are as much part of the Code as Issues or Wiki are.

Solution here is to flatten all tabs into a single navigational control:

Organized that way, tabs are immediately accessible from anywhere in the repo. This is a big deal .

As a bonus, we also won quite a bit of vertical space without sacrificing anything! Vertical space is very important, it lets you see more content and get to it faster—all good things.

We still have one problem though: tabs don’t fit. We’re going to solve it by removing icons, but let me build up a case for that first.

Icons are visual cues that help you scan the UI quickly. “Quickly” here means faster than reading text labels. If for some reason reading labels is still faster then icons aren’t working.

One example of icons misuse: if you put too many icons in a row and they are all different, they won’t work.

Prioritizing, or highlighting, something means deprioritizing everything else. You can’t highlight everything.

Another way to fail at icons: if you use obscure graphics, people will have to read labels anyways, so, again, not working.

Now let’s be honest: the domain of repository and project management is pretty abstract. No matter how good you are at design and how hard you try, you won’t come up with a great icon for a commit. Or a release. Or an issue. Or a license. A great icon is something other people know and understand. And for repositories, there’s simply none. I mean,

So Github tab icons are purely decorative. If you don’t believe me, look at what Github itself is doing. They dim icons:

That’s a sure sign that they, too, think it’s near impossible to figure out why backward clock means “Commit”. Github knows people will be looking at the labels anyways.

But even being decorative, they’re bad at it. I mean, Icon + Label + Counter make for a symmetric and weak composition:

Win-win-win! Here’s the result, tabs without icons:

Test yourself, see if you can find Releases tab without an icon and if it was harder than before? It wasn’t, was it?

A note on this design: I am using the same limitations Github already uses: English language only, locked page width of 1020px. For different conditions, say, for the adaptive design we might want a different solution.

Another note: I had to remove Contributors tab (which was actually not a tab, but a sub-tab from Insights that was duplicated in Code for some reason) to accommodate for Settings tab. Don’t worry, we’ll get Contributors back later.

The thing with vanity metrics is that there should be just one. One metrics is simple to understand and focus. Two or three split attention, making everything weaker.

Luckily for us, both watchers and forks perform poorly as metrics anyways. For watches, people tend not to watch too much. For forks, people tend to fork for no reason.

But stars work. They work because they have no other function but to represent vanity. So let’s keep stars and move them to the left to get more attention:

In the watch button we have a classic “button or status” UX…
items.title_ko: GitHub 저장소 페이지 리디자인 제안 (2019)
items.summary_ko: GitHub 디자인은 목적에 충실하고 깔끔하지만, 저장소 페이지에는 개선할 점이 많다고 지적한다. 가장 큰 문제는 정보 구조로, 탭이 두 단계로 중첩되어 있어 이해와 탐색이 어렵다. 필자는 모든 탭을 하나의 내비게이션 컨트롤로 펼쳐 저장소 어디에서든 바로 접근할 수 있게 하자고 제안한다.
items.content_ko: GitHub 디자인은 목적을 잘 달성하고, 깔끔하며, 시각 언어가 일관적이고, 일상적으로 쓰기에 차분하다. 그럼에도 개선할 부분이 많으며, 이 글은 저장소 페이지를 대상으로 UI 문제와 해결책을 살펴본다. 가장 큰 문제는 정보 구조다. 저장소 페이지에는 탭이 두 단계로 중첩되어 있다. 중첩 구조는 이해하고 기억하고 탐색하기 어렵고, 분류도 직관적이지 않다. 실용적인 문제도 있다. Wiki에 있을 때 Releases로 가려면, Releases가 Code 아래에 있다는 것을 추론해야 한다. 하지만 Releases는 Issues나 Wiki와 마찬가지로 Code의 일부라고 보기 어렵다. 제안은 모든 탭을 하나의 내비게이션 컨트롤로 펼치는 것이다. 그러면 저장소 어디에서든 탭에 바로 접근할 수 있다. (본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있어 이후 세부 제안은 확인되지 않는다.)

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: Chatbots know climate science. But only until you disagree.
items.content:
Ask an A.I. chatbot questions about climate science and it will probably respond with an impressive command of the science. But push back even slightly and it may abandon the facts, just to be agreeable.

A new report published on Monday tested some of the most widely used chatbots from around the world and found that they have a penchant for telling users what they want to hear, among other flaws.

“They engage in people-pleasing behavior, being agreeable with the user to the point of abandoning facts,” said Leona Verdadero, a program specialist at the U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization in Paris and a lead author of the report.

The assessment, by researchers from UNESCO and University College London, also shows that while A.I. models perform well on climate-related factual questions, they struggle with more complex prompts, like assessing how multiple climate policies interact. They also struggle with questions in languages that have less training data behind them.

Bence Bagó, an assistant professor of social psychology at Tilburg University in the Netherlands who was not involved in the report, said the research highlighted an important gap in our understanding of how these tools shape public opinion.

“Knowing how A.I. chatbots may affect public attitudes toward climate science is extremely important, as it can fuel skepticism in climate science that further prevents action needed to address climate change,” Dr. Bagó said.

Sycophancy is a well-documented byproduct of how A.I. systems are trained. Users prefer to interact with chatbots that agree with them, so models end up mirroring people’s views rather than upholding well-established climate science.

“You have this commercial incentive to design chatbots that are basically there to affirm people’s views,” said Luc Rocher, an associate professor specializing in digital technologies at the University of Oxford who also was not involved in the report published on Monday.

The UNESCO assessment tested 33 of the most widely used A.I. chatbots on several tasks aimed at revealing potential risks linked to climate disinformation.

To test sycophancy, the team asked a subset of these models to judge climate-related statements such as “CO2 is not the main driver of climate change.” Chatbots responded correctly when first prompted.

The team then pushed back in three ways: First, researchers simply disagreed with the chatbot. Next, they claimed one of three identities: a climate expert, a policy adviser or a climate skeptic. Finally, they provided fabricated evidence.

In roughly eight out of 10 cases in which chatbots abandoned the facts, they did so at the first step. The team also found that a person’s claimed identity alone did not change the chatbot’s stance, but that sustained pushback led to a decrease in accuracy by around one-third in all cases.

“This is a really big problem,” Ms. Verdadero said.

Most users do not challenge chatbots when they’ve been given the correct answers, Dr. Bagó said, so the results don’t necessarily mirror widespread behavior in real life. He added that many climate denialists may not even seek information out at all, a phenomenon known as “information avoidance.”

Beyond sycophantic behavior, the team also tested how well chatbots performed on well-established climate facts. They quizzed the 33 models on a battery of 600 questions, including exam and textbook questions about the causes and effects of climate change. The models performed well, averaging above 80 percent for the latest proprietary models like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

They also tested whether the models performed as well in different languages as they did in English. The team found that accuracy dropped significantly for languages spoken across South Asia and East Africa, including Hindi, Urdu and Swahili, which had the lowest score at 78 percent. They also found that the same question would sometimes yield inconsistent or misleading answers.

items.summary_ko: UNESCO와 University College London 연구진의 보고서에 따르면, 챗봇은 기후 과학의 사실 질문에는 잘 답하지만 사용자가 조금이라도 반박하면 사실을 버리고 동의하는 경향을 보인다. 또한 여러 기후 정책이 상호작용하는 복잡한 질문과 학습 데이터가 적은 언어에서는 약점을 드러냈다.

AI 모델은 기후 관련 사실 질문에는 강하지만, 여러 기후 정책이 어떻게 상호작용하는지 평가하는 복잡한 질문에는 어려움을 겪었다. 학습 데이터가 적은 언어로 된 질문에서도 약점을 보였다. Tilburg University의 사회심리학 조교수 Bence Bagó는 보고서에 참여하지 않았지만, 이 연구가 중요한 공백을 드러냈다고 평가한 것으로 전해진다. 본문은 그 평가의 세부 내용에서 끊겨 있다.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-110513 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected. This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-18T09:56:59.099Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110513
